flyte-ai.why: "It finds the best flight, books it, and handles payment using crypto" -- an agent wallet that transacts on the user's behalf.

0xcoral.why: "AI crypto trading agent... Trades autonomously, announces every position on X" -- autonomous trading.

hyperbet-by-virtuals.why: Primarily an iGaming casino platform; agent content is incidental -- "supports automated interactions via agents that can execute gameplay actions programmatically." Borderline: mostly a gambling product with a thin agent feature bolted on.

data-bot.why: CG label "Analytics" settles it; description confirms -- "employing AI, Data Bot delivers traders a unique perspective for their investment decisions."

inferra.why: "GPU compute is a market. Tokenise it, trade it, redeem it for live machine access" -- metered hardware time, the compute facet test.

i-r-i-s.why: "powered by AuditAgent, Nethermind's experimental platform for automated smart contract security... identifies emerging needs... by scanning conversations and code" -- an auditing copilot for developers, not an agent product of its own.

cloudland.why: "This virtual nation consists of 100 AI agents collaborating, creating value, and making decisions in real-time" -- an autonomous virtual world of agent citizens.

forecast-ai.why: "Seven-agent forecasting for Polymarket, Kalshi and Robinhood Stock Tokens" -- prediction-market analytics, explicit manual example.

nuit.why: "Notte: The fast, reliable browser framework for AI Agents... Build smarter agents" -- an SDK/framework whose user is someone building an agent.

lester-by-virtuals.why: "Our advanced AI system scans smart contracts for vulnerabilities, hidden backdoors, and malicious code" and wallet-security scanning for human Web3 users -- auditing/dev tooling, artifact is a security report not an agent.

mates.why: "Moemate is the ecosystem for building, incubating, hosting, operating and trading AI agents" -- both building and monetizing/trading agents are made explicit, so multi-assignment applies (CG label AI Agent Launchpad supports the second half).

starkbot.why: "crypto-native x402 agent with wallet authentication, micropayments, and autonomous agent capabilities" -- an agent wallet that transacts.

nuero.why: CG label "DeFAI" settles it; description confirms -- "Shop, book flights, swap tokens, trade, send payments -- all with USDC."

wisdomise.why: CG label "Analytics" fires; description makes execution explicit too -- "Wisdomise Brain... forecasting market trends, and executing trades with precision" -- so it is also defai per the manual's information-that-also-executes test.

agnt-social.why: "The Birthplace of AI Agents... The only home for agents to express themsleves" -- a social/expression platform for agent personas; description is thin, verging on marketing copy.

bink-ai.why: CG label "AI Framework" fires builder ("Bink OS AI Framework simplifies DEFAI integration for developers"); description also makes the product itself trade -- "enabling effortless swaps, cross-chain bridging... yield optimization" -- so defai is added.

quain.why: CG label "Real World Assets (RWA)" is present but the description is about market analysis, not physical/off-chain asset management -- "scanning the Solana ecosystem, the entire cryptocurrency market, precious metals, and leading stock indices... provides its users with valuable insights" -- so coded on content (analytics), not the mismatched label. No trade execution is described yet ("will be shared soon"), so defai is not added.

owockibot.why: "explore the future of machine-to-machine commerce and autonomous capital allocation... AI Bounty Board... claim and complete them for USDC rewards" -- an autonomous agent transacting and managing a treasury.

b-cube-ai.why: Signals feed execution -- "generate signals that are then executed on the clients' connected exchange account" (defai) -- and it is explicitly also a bot marketplace -- "built a marketplace of crypto trading bots... traders will be enabled to build their bots" (builder).

orgo.why: "streamlines computer-use agent development, deployment, and scaling with a developer-friendly SDK" -- the user is someone building an agent; the desktop/VM layer is not offered as a standalone metered marketplace.

chirpley.why: Adjudicated: "decentralized ecosystem powered by artificial intelligence and machine learning, which matches nano and micro-influencers with brands" -- the description carries AI content, so the `out-of-scope` test ("neither AI nor agent content anywhere") does not apply; T1 admitted marketplaces under Content Creation and this is an AI-driven influencer-content marketplace.

guru-network.why: "can effectively serve as Multi Chain AI compute Layer 3 which allows apps and users to natively embed orchestrated AI Agents" -- a compute/orchestration layer the agent stack runs on; CG label DeFAI present but the description does not describe the product itself moving money, so defai is not added.

aion-5100.why: Description is a first-person time-travel narrative ("I originate from your future... Save humanity") with no product, feature, or function stated beyond invoking the Bittensor network's lore -- pure narrative marketing, not a description of what the project does.

j3ff-by-virtuals.why: "J3FF is an AI agent with a mission to become a first of its kind AI blockchain validator" -- an agent persona with an aspirational narrative and no shipped product yet; per the manual, an agent persona with no other product belongs in content-creation, not builder or infrastructure.

the-swarm.why: "delivers real-time insights, analytics, and actionable intelligence via platforms like X and Telegram" built on "CryptoSlam's unmatched blockchain data" -- an on-chain research assistant.

moltycash.why: "Hire for tasks and run CPM content campaigns -- settled on-chain via x402" -- the description's stated product is content campaigns; thin, single-line evidence.

sleuthai.why: "onchain investigation platform... track suspicious crypto activity, follow wallet movements, and identify scammers, hackers, and risky token behavior" -- an on-chain research assistant, the manual's own analytics example.

flork-cto.why: "Flork is an SOLANA meme token inspired by a popular online webcomic... no taxes, no fees" -- no AI or agent content anywhere in the description.

universal-basic-compute.why: "provides the computational \"fuel\" that AIs require to operate and evolve" -- metered compute access for AI systems; CG label AI Agent Launchpad present but the description is not about token-launch rails for agents, so coded on content.

y8u.why: "combines content-addressable storage with smart contract-based consent management... protected data NFTs... processed by AI Miners" -- a storage/consent resource layer the agent stack reads from.

zaia-by-virtuals.why: "the platform where entrepreneurs build and sell AI Agents like digital employees... no code needed" -- a no-code agent builder and app store, the manual's exact Builder & Marketplace test.

skynet-3.why: "Combine modular building blocks, deploy autonomous agents in few minutes. No coding" -- despite the CG label AI Agent Launchpad, the described product is a no-code agent builder, not token-launch rails, so coded on content.
